chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): My zakat becomes due upon me for a month, so is it suitable for me to withhold a portion of it, fearing that someone who asks me may come, so that I have enough [to give]? He said: 'When the year passes, take it out from your wealth and do not mix it with anything else, and give it however you wish.'
I said: If I write it down and record it, will it be correct for me? He said: 'Yes, it will not harm you.'
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And it is permissible for him to send it to another country. That is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.حَالَ الْحَوْلُ: When the year passes (completion of the lunar year for zakat)

ai.seo_question: Can I keep my zakat money for a month after it becomes due to find a recipient?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility in zakat distribution, permitting the withholding of funds for a month post-due date to await suitable recipients, provided the wealth remains distinct and untainted by other assets. The permissibility of recording the amount and transferring it to another region underscores the practical adaptability of zakat obligations within Shia jurisprudence. This ruling highlights the emphasis on ensuring the effective and timely distribution of wealth to the deserving, rather than rigid adherence to immediate local disbursement.
